svg.title: This is a support-hit budget, in contrast to the single-anchor sum (AB7). Coefficients equal to zero still retain their addresses and eligibility predicates. For a finite set D of forced addresses, the gas term is zero unless their supports are pairwise disjoint and their inventories have union exactly Fθ(U); otherwise it is Q i∈D Ki(U). Summing these terms over finite D defines the forced gas. The regular exponent is the sum of 1Hθ(Xi)Ei. At a fixed finite torus these series are absolutely convergent: assign each regular term to its anchor and each forced term to one site of its nonempty support. Equations (AB7)–(AB10) bound their total envelope sums by |Λn|δ and |Λn|κ. The sum of absolute products over all finite subsets is at P most Q i ci. Restricting to compatible subsets only decreases it. If there are no flags, i(1 + ci) ≤e only the empty forced set can contribute, since each inventory is nonempty; the gas is then exactly one.
